summary: For the "Monuments of the Stars: Tales from the Martian Plains and Lunar Dust" project, we developed an engaging, narrative-driven digital book that brings NASA’s historic discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars back to life. To tackle the challenge, we personified iconic spacecraft like the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, the Opportunity rover, and the Viking 1 lander, sharing their historical missions and enduring legacies from a first-person perspective. This project directly addresses the challenge by educating school-age space enthusiasts about space exploration and the hardware that made groundbreaking science possible, turning cold metal into inspiring stories of discovery.
details:
Our project is a creative storytelling book ("Monuments of the Stars") that tells the historical missions of NASA’s discarded space hardware through the personal, emotional voices of the spacecraft themselves—the Apollo 11 Lunar Module ("Eagle") on the Moon, and the Opportunity rover and Viking 1 lander on Mars. Instead of dry technical reports, readers experience space history as a firsthand narrative of endurance, science, and discovery.

The main goal is to inspire school-age children and young space enthusiasts. By humanizing these robotic pioneers, we make space science, planetary conditions (like Martian dust storms), and aerospace history accessible, memorable, and deeply engaging for the next generation.

We used creative writing frameworks, historical mission data and logs provided by NASA archives, and digital publishing tools to structure and format our chapters.

We chose a first-person perspective ("I") to build an emotional bridge between historical space technology and young readers. Our team carefully balanced scientific accuracy—such as real locations (Mare Tranquillitatis, Meridiani Planum, Chryse Planitia), solar battery limits, and environmental conditions—with creative storytelling to spark curiosity and imagination.
